answer: A marble-trading agent earns voting weight by proving storage of a large dataset sealed to its key. A slow, key-specific cipher prevents sharing one sealed replica across aliases. The zephyr beacon selects fresh block challenges after commitment; verifiers check proofs before a deadline too short to reseal. Missing proofs suspend voting. A thousand identities can run in parallel but need a thousand replicas, so disk costs scale with weight. This relies on a sound proof-of-replication construction with verifiable sealing.
